summary: Shoshone National Forest lookout north of Cody, built 1912-13 with a telephone line to Cody; listed as gone, removal undated, site today undescribed.

facts.design: 8-by-8-foot log cab (firelookout.com: on a 10-foot log base)
facts.status_note: Listed as gone; no source describes what remains on the peak now

events.note: Material hauled from Cody from September 1912; station completed by November 1913
August 1914 item says Arthur Braten left for Crandall Creek and would take the work at a Lookout Station; the peak is not named

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1912 plan was an eight-foot-square cabin. The 1913 paper gives a 13-by-13-foot building with an 8-by-8-foot tower; firelookout.com gives a 10-foot log base with an 8-by-8-foot cab. Both put an 8-by-8-foot cab on top, but the base size is described differently and the sources do not reconcile it.

sources.title: Hunters Peak (Forest Lookouts, western US), quoting the Park County Enterprise

notes_for_editor: The 1912-1914 history comes from Park County Enterprise items as quoted on the westlookouts page; the original paper was not checked. Staffing is planned in the 1913 items and only one 1914 item (Arthur Braten, who left for Crandall Creek to take the work at a Lookout Station) suggests staff; that item does not name the peak, so the staffed event is hedged. A Cody Journal biography of Evelyn Braten covers Windy Mountain, not this peak, and was not used. No removal date and no description of the site today were found. Dimensions conflict between the 1913 paper and firelookout.com (see resolved_conflicts). The elevation 9,037 ft on firelookout.com could fill elevation_m if the editor wants it.
